concept.name: Bollinger bandwidth
concept.definition: A Bollinger-derived indicator measuring the percentage width between the upper and lower bands relative to the middle band, tracking volatility expansion and contraction on a normalized scale comparable across securities and timeframes.
concept.intuition: It turns the visual 'pinch' of the bands into a number: falling BandWidth means volatility is drying up; the famous Squeeze is BandWidth at the low end of its own historical range.
concept.mechanics: Compute (Upper - Lower) / Middle x 100 from the Bollinger Bands (default 20, 2). Narrowness is judged against the indicator's own 6-12 month range; the Squeeze alerts to coming volatility, and the direction comes from the subsequent band break.
concept.failure_modes: 'Narrow' is relative to each security's own history, so thresholds do not transfer between instruments; the Squeeze is directionless and the first band break after a squeeze can fail.
concept.misconceptions: A low BandWidth does not guarantee an imminent big move - volatility can stay compressed for months, and low-volatility securities always show lower BandWidth than volatile ones.
concept.example: Upper 53, lower 47, middle 50: BandWidth = (53-47)/50 x 100 = 12; StockCharts' Alaska Airlines squeeze triggered below a BandWidth of 10.
